diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says OUT, datasheet reading says GND
diffs.evidence: The M5Stack PinMap lists the HY2.0-4P wires as 'Black Red Yellow White PORT.B GND 5V NC Digital Output'; the UNIT_BUTTON V1.0 schematic (J1 'Grove') puts the button/R1 10k/R2 20k signal net on J1 pin 1, nothing on pin 2, VCC on pin 3 and GND on pin 4, and on HY2.0 cables white is pin 1 and black pin 4, so the second reading listed the wire-colour table (black first) as if it were pin 1 to 4; the model pin order (pin 1 OUT (white), 2 NC (yellow), 3 5V (red), 4 GND (black)) is correct.

diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 4.5 V, datasheet reading 5 V
diffs.evidence: The vendor page gives only the nominal port voltage ('PORT.B GND 5V NC Digital Output') with no minimum; the unit is passive (button, 10k/20k divider, 100 nF per the schematic), so 4.5 V is the model's tolerance for a sagging USB 5 V rail (high level still about 3.0 V), not a contradiction of the nominal 5 V.

diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 5.25 V, datasheet reading 5 V
diffs.evidence: The vendor page gives only the nominal port voltage ('PORT.B GND 5V NC Digital Output') and no maximum; with the schematic's 10k/20k divider, 5.25 V gives a 3.5 V high level, which stays within a 3.3 V GPIO VDD+0.3 V limit, so 5.25 V is a conservative ceiling around the nominal 5 V rather than an error.
